meta.title: Who originally recorded "Love Hurts"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not Nazareth. The Everly Brothers recorded Love Hurts in July 1960 as an album track on Warner Bros. Boudleaux Bryant wrote it; it was never their single.
meta.ogDescription: Not Nazareth. The Everly Brothers cut it in July 1960 for A Date with the Everly Brothers. Boudleaux Bryant wrote it. Nazareth's 1974 cover made it famous.

answer.label: Not a Nazareth original — a 1960 Everly Brothers album track
answer.originalArtistDates: Don Everly 1937-2021 · Phil Everly 1939-2014 · American close-harmony duo
answer.sourceLine: Nazareth’s thunderous 1974 power ballad is so total a performance that the song reads as a Scottish hard-rock original. It isn’t. “Love Hurts” was written by Nashville songwriter Boudleaux Bryant and first recorded by The Everly Brothers in July 1960, then buried as track seven on their Warner Bros. album A Date with the Everly Brothers in October of that year. It was never issued as an Everly single — a dispute with their manager and publisher Wesley Rose kept it off the 45s — so the version that made the song famous in America was a cover recorded on the other side of the Atlantic.

original.heading: Who recorded it first
original.label: Warner Bros.
original.released: Recorded July 1960 and released in October 1960 as track seven on A Date with the Everly Brothers (Warner Bros. Records, catalogue W 1395). It was never issued as a single or a B-side.
original.charted: Did not chart — it was never a single. The album around it reached No. 9 on the US Billboard chart and No. 3 in the UK.
original.cover: Nazareth’s power-ballad version, released as a single on 8 November 1974 (Mooncrest in the UK, A&M in the US and Canada) and later the closing track on Hair of the Dog, reached No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 1 in Canada, the Netherlands, Belgium, Norway and South Africa.

trail: The original sits on the Everlys’ second Warner Bros. album, A Date with the Everly Brothers ↗, released in October 1960 — a record whose single, “Cathy’s Clown,” had already come out that April.

Roy Orbison took it to RCA Victor Studio B in Nashville on 27 February 1961 and put it out as the B-side of “Running Scared,” where it reached No. 5 in Australia — one of several stops charted on the song’s version history ↗.
Nazareth ↗, formed in Dunfermline in December 1968, released their version as a single on 8 November 1974; it became their only US Top Ten hit and the definitive reading for most listeners since.
Jim Capaldi’s version, released in November 1975, went to No. 4 in the UK — his highest-charting British single — and Cher recorded it twice, in 1975 and again in 1991.

authors.name: The Everly Brothers
authors.heading: The Everly Brothers
authors.metaLine: Don Everly 1937-2021 and Phil Everly 1939-2014 - American close-harmony duo
authors.bio: Don and Phil Everly recorded “Love Hurts” in July 1960 and released it that October on A Date with the Everly Brothers, their second album for Warner Bros. They had already reshaped popular music with “Bye Bye Love” and “Wake Up Little Susie,” and their close two-part harmony ran straight into The Beatles, The Beach Boys and Simon & Garfunkel. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in its inaugural 1986 class and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2001.

authors.name: Nazareth
authors.heading: Nazareth
authors.metaLine: Formed December 1968 in Dunfermline, Scotland - hard rock band
authors.bio: Nazareth cut “Love Hurts” as a slow-burning power ballad, Dan McCafferty’s sandpaper rasp doing the work the Everlys’ harmony had done. Released as a single on 8 November 1974 and later collected on 1975’s Hair of the Dog, it reached No. 8 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and went to No. 1 in Canada, the Netherlands, Belgium, Norway and South Africa. It remains the band’s only US Top Ten hit, and the only version of the song ever to be a US hit single. The record is genuinely great; the only error is chronological.

authors.name: Boudleaux Bryant
authors.heading: Boudleaux Bryant
authors.bio: Boudleaux Bryant wrote “Love Hurts” alone; Acuff-Rose Publications registered it on 30 August 1960. With his wife Felice he formed one of the most successful songwriting partnerships in American music, credited with some 6,000 compositions and responsible for much of the Everly Brothers’ catalogue, including “Bye Bye Love,” “Wake Up Little Susie” and “All I Have to Do Is Dream,” as well as “Rocky Top.” The Bryants were inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 1986 and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1991.

misattribution.heading: Right band, wrong origin
misattribution.intro: Nazareth’s 1974 recording is the one nearly everybody has heard, and it is often taken to be where the song began. The chronology says otherwise.

items.who: Nazareth wrote and originated “Love Hurts” in 1974.
items.why: Theirs is the only version ever to be a US hit single — No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 — and the arrangement is so distinctive it sounds authored rather than covered.
Issued that October as an album track on A Date with the Everly Brothers (Warner Bros., W 1395). Never released as a single, so it never charted in its own right.
Published by Acuff-Rose Publications on 30 August 1960. Bryant also wrote “Bye Bye Love” and “All I Have to Do Is Dream” for the same duo.
Cut at RCA Victor Studio B in Nashville and released as the flip of “Running Scared,” reaching No. 5 in Australia — another reason the song was already in circulation long before 1974.

misattribution.truthLine: Written by Boudleaux Bryant, first recorded by The Everly Brothers in July 1960 — and made famous by Nazareth fourteen years after the fact.

context.heading: Why the cover swallowed the original
lead: The interesting question is not why Nazareth’s version was big — it is why the Everlys’ version was invisible. It was never a single. It sat seventh on the second side of an album whose commercial job had already been done by “Cathy’s Clown,” and the Everlys’ relationship with their publisher, Wesley Rose of Acuff-Rose, soured badly enough that Rose cut them off from the Bryants’ catalogue between 1961 and 1964. A song with no 45, no promotion and a broken supply line behind it does not become anybody’s idea of the definitive recording.

Meanwhile the song kept travelling as a B-side and an album cut. Roy Orbison recorded it at RCA Victor Studio B in Nashville on 27 February 1961 and it went out as the flip of “Running Scared,” reaching No. 5 in Australia. Jim Capaldi’s reading, released in November 1975, hit No. 4 in the UK — his highest-charting British single. But only Nazareth’s took it into the American Top Ten, and in the pre-internet decades the hit single is what a song’s history collapses into.
detailsBody: 30 August 1960 — Boudleaux Bryant’s composition is published by Acuff-Rose Publications.
July 1960 — The Everly Brothers record “Love Hurts” during the sessions for their second Warner Bros. album.
October 1960 — The recording is issued as an album track on A Date with the Everly Brothers (Warner Bros. W 1395). It is never released as a single.
27 February 1961 — Roy Orbison records the song at RCA Victor Studio B, Nashville; it appears as the B-side of “Running Scared” and reaches No. 5 in Australia.
8 November 1974 — Nazareth release their power-ballad version as a single (Mooncrest in the UK, A&M in the US and Canada).
April 1975 — Hair of the Dog is released; “Love Hurts” closes the international and US editions.
1976 — Nazareth’s single reaches No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100, the band’s only US Top Ten hit.
context.pull: No single, no promotion — just track seven, waiting.

listen.what: The Everly Brothers’ 1960 recording, as it appears on A Date with the Everly Brothers.
listen.source: An auto-generated “Provided to YouTube by Rhino/Warner Records” upload on the official “The Everly Brothers - Topic” channel. The description names the album A Date with The Everly Brothers and carries a ℗ 1960 Warner Records Inc. line, and the 2:22 runtime matches the MusicBrainz recording for the 1960 Warner Bros. release — so this is the original master, remastered, not a later re-recording.

listenCover.what: Nazareth’s 1974 power-ballad rebuild, produced by Manny Charlton with Dan McCafferty’s rasp on lead — the version that ran away from the Everlys’ gentle 1960 original.
listenCover.source: Auto-generated upload on “Nazareth - Topic”: “Provided to YouTube by Universal Music Group”, ℗ 1975 A&M Records, from Hair Of The Dog, crediting producer Manny Charlton and vocalist Dan McCafferty. Runtime 233s (3:53), sitting dead centre of the MusicBrainz cluster of 3:51-3:54 for the studio track. One note: this is the Hair of the Dog album master (℗ 1975 A&M, the US pressing) rather than the 8 Nov 1974 Mooncrest single artefact — the same recording, and the Salvo-distributed “Single Edit” upload (1VGbnKGRxMc) runs 232s, within a second, so the two are functionally identical. Avoided the 4:36 Homecoming live cut MusicBrainz also lists.
